changes: Export public cj.feval with callable, extra argument, endpoint, side and composition dispatch.
Quasimatrix evaluation supports endpoints and side flags. Empty queries keep their input shape. Matrix and tensor evaluation concatenates along axis 1 before applying row orientation once.
Quasimatrix.isempty follows native array and first-column semantics.
All 13 native isempty predicates are represented, using literal pi and horizontal concatenation. Unbounded predicates 11–13 reuse the exact feval 32/33/35 constructors.
baseline_evidence: Corrected quasimatrix baseline: one pass, four failures (transposed shape, empty shape, endpoints, missing isempty). Earlier component-last matrix expectations were rejected.
Root literal native isempty predicate 9 exposed missing Quasimatrix.isempty. An initial adaptive callback surrogate had hidden it and was replaced by actual horizontal concatenation.

qualification.final_test_formatting: Only import order and trailing whitespace changed after the combined gate; non-import test AST unchanged.
qualification.source: Publication source byte-identical to guarded source; tail tests byte-identical to qualified isolated tests. The public wrapper does not change existing entry points.

supplemental_bounds: New quasimatrix analytic controls use 20 eps * max(1, expected scale), not an original MATLAB test bound. Existing assertion bounds are unchanged. Public wrapper controls use exact arrays or 4 eps / 10 eps analytic bounds.
compatibility: Python scalar and rank-one component-last conventions are retained; row Q rank-one evaluation returns (ncols, npoints).
Column endpoint results retain the Python vector convention; row endpoints return (ncols, 1).
limitations: Empty Chebfun evaluation remains open in a separate candidate.
JIT subnormal routing and nonfinite boundaries remain in a separate candidate.
Full native API, assertions, pages, figures, performance and current-main CI remain incomplete.
